title: Positioning Vygotsky for inclusive education: A psycho-philosophical context
abstract: Inclusion has its roots in two foundational ideas: equity and a rights-based perspective on education, as articulated in national and global policies. However, inclusion, in its true sense, has been misunderstood as helping learners adjust to the mainstream. This misleading idea has raised serious concerns about the essential role of diversity in inclusion. In its narrow terms, the physical arrangements for learners with disabilities have been accepted as inclusion, thereby overlooking the underlying assumptions about development, learning, and diversity that actually shape the discourse of inclusive educational practices. This makes it imperative to lay out the theoretical and philosophical foundations of inclusive education. Vygotsky, while avoiding individualistic and deficit-driven approaches, reframes cognitive engagement as socially mediated and culturally situated processes. Considering diversity an opportunity rather than a barrier in the classroom, Vygotsky emphasises dialectical materialism and the social origins of higher mental processes as vital to cognitive practices. In this context, this discourse analysis-based article revisits the core constructs of Vygotskian theory, such as co-construction, mediation via cultural tools, internalisation, perezhivanie, the Zone of Proximal Development, and the shaping of thought with language, to conceptualise inclusive education within this framework. This conceptualisation indicates the positioning of certain essentialities, such as dialogue, scaffolding, collaboration, and interaction with peers, in creating inclusive educational opportunities for all learners. The article also explores the potential to apply Vygotsky’s ideas to pedagogical processes, assessment, and teacher preparation, focusing on teachers' roles as mediators in developing supportive, collaborative learning environments. The article concludes by establishing the strength of Vygotsky’s theoretical framework in shaping the scope of inclusive education.
